meta.subject: DATA_SCIENCE
meta.author: bank-team-data-science
meta.attestation: authored from first principles; no protected content used

questions.topic: What makes a pipeline a pipeline
questions.learningObjective: Define what makes a pipeline a pipeline
questions.stem: Cartographer Vera asks what turns a script into a pipeline; which trait?

options.text: Automated, repeatable flow from source to destination

questions.explanation: A pipeline is an automated, repeatable flow moving data from source to destination.

questions.stem: Cartographer needs results every 24 hours with large volume; which mode?
questions.explanation: Large volume on a daily cadence suits batch processing.

questions.topic: What a late record does to a window
questions.learningObjective: Explain effect of a late record on a window
questions.stem: A late record arrives after a window closes; what happens to aggregates?

answer.exemplar: The late record is dropped or routed to a side output, so the window aggregate does not include it unless the window is reprocessed.

questions.explanation: Late records miss the closed window and are dropped or side-output, excluding them from aggregates.

questions.stem: An idempotent write processes the same record twice; how many rows written?
questions.explanation: Idempotent writes produce the same result no matter how many times applied, so only 1 row remains.

questions.stem: Out-of-order events arrive; watermark advances; what determines lateness?
questions.explanation: Lateness is determined by comparing event time to the watermark threshold.

questions.topic: A schema change and the consumer it breaks
questions.learningObjective: Identify consumer broken by schema change
questions.stem: Cartographer adds a required field to an event schema; which consumer breaks?

options.text: Consumers expecting the old schema without the field

questions.explanation: Consumers coded against the old schema break when a new required field appears.

questions.learningObjective: State what a data contract declares
questions.stem: A data contract between producer and consumer; what does it state?

options.text: Schema, semantics, and SLAs for the data

questions.explanation: A data contract declares schema, semantics, and service levels for shared data.

questions.topic: What a data quality test can express
questions.stem: Cartographer writes a data quality test asserting all ids are unique; what does it express?

answer.exemplar: It expresses an invariant that the id column must contain no duplicates, failing the pipeline if any duplicate id is found.

questions.explanation: A uniqueness test expresses an invariant that ids must have no duplicates.

questions.stem: Freshness threshold 60 minutes; data last updated 90 minutes ago; how many minutes stale?
questions.explanation: Data is 30 minutes past the 60-minute threshold, so it is 30 minutes stale.

questions.topic: What a row-count check cannot see
questions.stem: Row-count check passes but data is wrong; what can it not see?

options.misconception: not its job but not core

questions.explanation: Row count only counts rows; it cannot verify values inside them.

questions.stem: Null-rate check on a column; what does it detect?

options.text: Share of rows with null values in that column

questions.explanation: Null-rate check measures the share of rows with nulls in the column.

questions.stem: Pipeline task fails; alerting should trigger on which signal?

options.text: Task failure status or error log

questions.explanation: Alerting triggers on failure status or error logs, not success metrics.

questions.stem: Cartographer retries a failed write; what risk arises?

answer.exemplar: Retrying a non-idempotent write risks duplicate rows or double counting if the original actually succeeded.

questions.explanation: Retrying non-idempotent writes can create duplicates if the first attempt partially succeeded.

questions.topic: Why a backfill needs its own path
questions.learningObjective: Explain why backfill needs separate path
questions.stem: Backfill processes 1000 historical rows; normal path handles 10 per second. Seconds if using normal path?
questions.explanation: 1000 rows at 10 per second takes 100 seconds, too slow for normal path.

questions.topic: End-to-end time of a staged pipeline
questions.stem: Stages take 5, 10, and 15 minutes sequentially; end-to-end time?
questions.explanation: Sequential stages sum: 5 + 10 + 15 = 30 minutes.

questions.topic: How far past target a table is
questions.stem: Target 1000 rows, actual 1250; how far past target?
questions.explanation: Actual minus target: 1250 - 1000 = 250 rows past target.

questions.stem: Null rate moved from 2% to 5%; percentage point increase?
questions.explanation: 5% minus 2% equals 3 percentage points increase.

questions.learningObjective: Compute deviation a count check tolerates
questions.stem: Count check tolerates 5% deviation on 1000 expected rows; allowed range?

answer.exemplar: The check allows between 950 and 1050 rows, since 5% of 1000 is 50 rows either side of the expected count.

questions.explanation: 5% of 1000 is 50, so allowed range is 950 to 1050 rows.

questions.learningObjective: Compute rows written by repeated delivery
questions.stem: Non-idempotent delivery sends same 10 rows three times; rows written?
questions.explanation: Three deliveries of 10 rows each write 30 rows when not idempotent.

questions.stem: Canary gets 5% of 2000 requests; how many requests?
questions.explanation: 5% of 2000 is 100 requests for the canary.

questions.topic: What makes a pipeline a pipeline
questions.learningObjective: Evaluate a manual script as pipeline
questions.stem: Cartographer runs a manual SQL script weekly; is it a pipeline?

options.text: No, SQL cannot be a pipeline
Yes, any SQL script is a pipeline

questions.explanation: A manual script lacks automation, so it is not a pipeline despite periodic execution.

questions.stem: Cartographer needs sub-second alerts on events; which mode?
questions.explanation: Sub-second alerting requires streaming, not batch.

questions.topic: What a late record does to a window
questions.stem: Late record arrives after window; cartographer wants it counted; options?

answer.exemplar: Allow late data with a grace period or reprocess the window so the late record is included in the aggregate.

questions.explanation: A grace period or reprocessing lets late records be included in window aggregates.

questions.stem: Upsert same record 5 times; how many rows in table?
questions.explanation: Upsert is idempotent, so 5 applications leave 1 row.

questions.stem: Larger watermark delay; what tradeoff?

options.text: More late data included, higher latency

questions.explanation: Larger delay includes more late data but increases result latency.

questions.topic: A schema change and the consumer it breaks
questions.stem: Adding an optional field with default; is it backward compatible?

options.text: No, any field addition breaks consumers
Yes, old consumers ignore unknown optional fields

questions.explanation: Optional fields with defaults are backward compatible for old consumers.

questions.stem: Producer violates data contract; what should happen?

options.text: Pipeline fails or alerts on contract violation

questions.explanation: Contract violations should fail the pipeline or alert, not be silently ignored.

questions.topic: What a data quality test can express
questions.learningObjective: Evaluate a data quality test scope
questions.stem: Data quality test checks row count only; can it catch bad values?

answer.exemplar: No, a row-count test only verifies quantity, not correctness of values, so bad values pass unnoticed.

questions.explanation: Row-count tests verify quantity only and miss bad values.

questions.stem: Freshness threshold 30 min; data 45 min old; minutes over threshold?
questions.explanation: 45 - 30 = 15 minutes over the freshness threshold.

questions.topic: What a row-count check cannot see
questions.learningObjective: Create a value-level check beyond row count
questions.stem: Row count passes but values wrong; cartographer wants value checks; approach?

options.text: Add column-level quality tests like not-null and ranges

questions.explanation: Column-level tests on nulls and ranges catch bad values that row count misses.

questions.stem: Cartographer wants to alert when null rate exceeds 5%; how?
questions.explanation: A quality test asserting null rate <= 5% automates the alert.

questions.stem: Cartographer wants on-call paged on pipeline failure; which signal?
questions.explanation: Task failure events should route to the on-call pager.

questions.stem: Cartographer wants safe retries; what must the write be?

answer.exemplar: The write must be idempotent, using upserts or deduplication keys, so retries do not create duplicates.

questions.explanation: Idempotent writes make retries safe by preventing duplicates.

questions.topic: Why a backfill needs its own path
questions.stem: Backfill of 5000 rows at 50 per second via normal path takes seconds; better dedicated path at 500 per second?
questions.explanation: 5000 divided by 500 equals 10 seconds on the dedicated path.

questions.topic: End-to-end time of a staged pipeline
questions.learningObjective: Create parallel stages to reduce e2e time
questions.stem: Three stages 5,10,15 min can run in parallel; e2e time?
questions.explanation: Parallel stages finish when the longest completes: max(5,10,15)=15 minutes.

questions.topic: How far past target a table is
questions.learningObjective: Create an alert for past-target deviation
questions.stem: Cartographer wants alert when table exceeds target by 10%; which check?

options.text: Quality test comparing actual to 110% of target

questions.explanation: A quality test comparing actual to 110% of target raises the alert.

questions.stem: Cartographer wants to track null rate over time; which approach?

options.text: Log null rate per run and chart trend

questions.explanation: Logging null rate per run and charting the trend reveals movement over time.

questions.stem: Cartographer tightens count tolerance from 5% to 1%; effect on false positives?

answer.exemplar: Tightening tolerance from 5% to 1% increases false positives because normal variance may exceed the stricter threshold.

questions.explanation: Stricter tolerance catches more deviations but raises false positives from normal variance.

questions.stem: Deduplication reduces 30 repeated rows to distinct count 10; rows removed?
questions.explanation: 30 repeated rows minus 10 distinct rows equals 20 rows removed.

questions.stem: Cartographer routes 1% of 50000 requests to canary; requests?
questions.explanation: 1% of 50000 is 500 requests for the canary.

questions.topic: What makes a pipeline a pipeline
questions.learningObjective: Analyze a batch job as pipeline
questions.stem: A nightly ETL job with extract, transform, load; is it a pipeline?

options.text: No, only streaming is a pipeline
No, ETL is not a pipeline

questions.explanation: An automated nightly ETL is a pipeline despite being batch.

questions.learningObjective: Analyze cost of streaming for batch workload
questions.stem: Streaming a daily batch workload; main drawback?

options.text: Higher cost and complexity for no latency benefit

questions.explanation: Streaming a daily batch adds cost and complexity without latency benefit.

questions.topic: What a late record does to a window
questions.stem: Late record beyond allowed lateness; where does it go?

answer.exemplar: It is dropped or sent to a side output for separate handling, keeping the main window result stable.

questions.explanation: Overly late records are dropped or side-output to protect window results.

questions.stem: Idempotent write partially fails after writing 3 of 10 rows; rows after retry?
questions.explanation: Idempotent retry ensures final state has all 10 rows despite partial failure.

questions.stem: Watermark is max event time minus 5 min; latest event 10:00; watermark?
questions.explanation: Watermark is 10:00 minus 5 minutes = 09:55.

questions.topic: A schema change and the consumer it breaks
questions.stem: Cartographer removes a field from schema; which consumer breaks?
questions.explanation: Consumers depending on the removed field break.

questions.stem: Data contract version increments from v1 to v2; what should consumers do?

options.text: Adapt to new contract or stay on v1

questions.explanation: Consumers either adapt to v2 or remain on v1 per compatibility policy.

questions.topic: What a data quality test can express
questions.stem: Can a data quality test express a business rule like valid status codes?

answer.exemplar: Yes, a quality test can assert that status values belong to an allowed set, expressing the business rule as an invariant.

questions.explanation: Quality tests can express business rules as invariants such as allowed value sets.

questions.stem: Freshness check threshold 60 min; data 55 min old; minutes under threshold?
questions.explanation: 60 - 55 = 5 minutes under the threshold.

questions.topic: What a row-count check cannot see
questions.stem: Row count correct but duplicates present; what is missed?
questions.explanation: Row count cannot detect that duplicates distort the meaning of the count.

questions.stem: Null rate spikes suddenly; likely cause?
questions.explanation: A sudden null-rate spike usually indicates upstream sending nulls.

questions.stem: Too many low-severity alerts; what is the risk?

options.text: Alert fatigue causing ignored critical alerts

questions.explanation: Excessive alerts cause fatigue, leading to ignored critical alerts.

questions.stem: Retrying all failed tasks immediately; what risk?

answer.exemplar: Immediate retries can create a retry storm, overwhelming the downstream system and causing further failures.

questions.explanation: Immediate retries can overwhelm downstream systems, causing retry storms.

questions.topic: Why a backfill needs its own path
questions.stem: Backfill consumes 80% of DB capacity; production needs 50%; headroom?
questions.explanation: 80% plus 50% exceeds 100%, leaving zero headroom, so backfill and production conflict.

questions.topic: End-to-end time of a staged pipeline
questions.stem: Stages 5, 20, 5 min sequential; which is bottleneck?
questions.explanation: The longest stage at 20 minutes is the bottleneck.

questions.topic: How far past target a table is
questions.stem: Table grows 10% past target each week; what does trend indicate?
questions.explanation: Consistent growth past target indicates unbounded growth needing intervention.

questions.stem: Null rate drops from 8% to 3%; what likely improved?
questions.explanation: A drop in null rate suggests improved upstream data completeness.

questions.stem: Wider tolerance on count check; what is the effect on detection?

answer.exemplar: Wider tolerance reduces false positives but may miss real anomalies that fall within the expanded range.

questions.explanation: Wider tolerance reduces false positives but can miss real anomalies.

questions.stem: Without dedup, 4 deliveries of 25 rows each; rows stored?
questions.explanation: 4 deliveries times 25 rows equals 100 rows stored without dedup.

questions.stem: Canary receives 2% of traffic and fails; blast radius?
questions.explanation: Canary blast radius is limited to its 2% traffic share.
